nodes.label: imagegen-frontend-mobile Skill
nodes.rationale: Scoped to image generation only (never code) because mixing implementation output with art direction was observed to collapse premium mobile concepts into generic templated screens.

nodes.label: Active Baseline Configuration (Mobile Dials)
nodes.rationale: Numeric dials (DESIGN_VARIANCE 8, VISUAL_DENSITY 3, CLARITY_DISCIPLINE 10, etc.) encode taste as adjustable defaults so the brief can override them without rewriting the skill.

nodes.label: Platform Mode Rule (iOS / Android / Cross-platform)
nodes.rationale: One dominant platform feel must be chosen first; mixing iOS and Android patterns produces incoherent, non-native-feeling screens.

nodes.label: Generate Enough Screens Rule
nodes.rationale: Multiple clean readable screens beat one compressed board with tiny unreadable text; screen count must never be reduced for convenience.

nodes.label: Do Not Crop Old Images Rule
nodes.rationale: Cropping distorts spacing, proportions and typography, so a fresh standalone render is preferred over cutouts.

nodes.label: App Design Bible Rule
nodes.rationale: An internal locked design bible (palette, type, radius, icon style, navigation model) prevents screen 3-5 from drifting into a different app.

nodes.label: Logical Flow Rule
nodes.rationale: A screen set should read as a real product walkthrough, so each screen must be justified by the navigation action that reaches it.

nodes.label: Device Mockup Frame Rule
nodes.rationale: A visible phone frame is default because it grounds the render as an app rather than a poster, but CONTENT_FIRST_MOCKUP_BALANCE keeps the frame supporting rather than dominating.

nodes.label: Safe Area and System Region Rule
First Screen Cleanliness Rule
nodes.rationale: The first viewport carries the product impression, so a single focal point and one clear CTA beat stat/chip/pill density.

nodes.label: Mobile Style Variation Engine
nodes.rationale: Forcing one pick per category (theme, typography, structure, imagery, texture, palette, 4 components, 2 assets, 2 motion cues) breaks repetitive default output through committed combinatorial choice.

nodes.label: Mobile Color Palette Rule
nodes.rationale: Default purple-blue AI palettes and random saturated color are banned because they are the strongest signal of generated, template-grade design.

nodes.label: Background Texture and Surface Rule
nodes.rationale: Texture should support mood, not compete with the interface — sterile flat backgrounds read as generic, heavy noise destroys readability.

nodes.label: Image-Behind-Text Rule
nodes.rationale: Fades, scrims and masks are mandated so imagery can bleed behind typography without sacrificing legibility.

nodes.label: Mobile Iconography Rule
nodes.rationale: Lucide-like default icon packs make apps read as templates, so a custom-feeling, brand-appropriate icon system is required.

nodes.label: Mobile Anti-AI-Tells Rule
nodes.rationale: Catalogues visual, layout, copy and clutter tells (purple-blue gradients, fake chart spam, 'elevate your life', fake brands like Acme/NovaCore) so they can be actively negated.

nodes.label: Text Size and Readability Rule
nodes.rationale: If the text feels small the design is unfinished; readability outranks cleverness, density and decorative small type.

nodes.label: Not Always Simple Rule (Clean over Minimal)
nodes.rationale: Cleanliness rather than simplicity is the goal, so richer layered screens are allowed provided hierarchy stays readable.

nodes.label: One Horizontal Image Per Section Rule
nodes.rationale: Explicitly overrides the model's default urge to collapse a page into one tall image, because per-section frames stay high-fidelity and codeable.

nodes.label: Hero Composition Bias
nodes.rationale: Left-text / right-image is named the single most overused AI hero pattern, so it is demoted from default to last resort with a pre-output habit check.

nodes.label: Brief-to-Direction Mapping
nodes.rationale: The user's brief always overrides dial defaults; recipes must never be forced against an explicit request for restraint or atmosphere.

nodes.label: Combinatorial Variation Engine
nodes.rationale: Choose one option per category and commit — mashing everything together yields chaos, repeating defaults yields AI-looking output.

nodes.label: Hero Scale (Giant / Mid / Mini)
nodes.rationale: Mini does not mean weak — it means confident restraint; the scale must be chosen decisively rather than split down the middle.

nodes.label: Second-Read Moment
nodes.rationale: Exactly one unobvious motif per page — it must aid scan order or brand recall, never be gimmick-for-gimmick.

nodes.label: Frontend Reference Rule (Codeability)
nodes.rationale: Every image must let a developer or coding model infer layout, hierarchy, spacing and CTA priority — abstract mood art fails the purpose.

nodes.label: Anti-AI-Slop Rules
nodes.rationale: Groups slop by axis (layout, visual, typography, content, density, marquee, KPI) so each can be independently policed.

nodes.label: Palette Discipline (1 primary / 1 secondary / 1 accent)
nodes.rationale: Section-level mood shifts must reuse one palette; a full theme swap per section destroys brand recall across per-section frames.

nodes.label: Gradient Discipline
nodes.rationale: Separates professional low-chroma palette-matched grades (encouraged) from AI gradient slop (rainbow mesh, purple-to-blue, neon halos, gradient text).

nodes.label: Multi-Image Consistency Rule
nodes.rationale: Because each section is generated separately, brand recall must be enforced explicitly; anything breaking recall counts as over-variation.

nodes.label: Composition Variety Check
nodes.rationale: Reject the set if one anchor repeats 3 sections in a row or one background mode repeats 4; suspended entirely for minimalist briefs where restraint is the design.

nodes.label: Conversion Focus (hook / proof / educate / convert)
nodes.rationale: Every section has a job so artistic pages still read as real product sites rather than pure mood reels with no funnel logic.

nodes.label: industrial-brutalist-ui Skill
nodes.rationale: Deliberately discards conventional consumer UI patterns to project raw functionality, mechanical precision, and high data density.

nodes.label: Swiss Industrial Print Archetype
nodes.rationale: Light newsprint substrate (#F4F4F0 / #EAE8E3) with carbon ink foreground, derived from 1960s corporate identity systems and machinery blueprints.

nodes.label: Tactical Telemetry & CRT Terminal Archetype
nodes.rationale: Dark-mode-exclusive (#0A0A0A, never pure #000000) with white phosphor foreground; pure black is avoided because a deactivated CRT is never truly black.

nodes.label: Single-Archetype Commitment Rule
nodes.rationale: One substrate palette per project; mixing light and dark substrates inside one interface breaks the illusion of a single physical medium.

nodes.label: Macro-Typography (Structural Headers)
nodes.rationale: Negative tracking (-0.03em to -0.06em) and compressed leading (0.85-0.95) force glyphs to fuse into solid architectural blocks.

nodes.label: Micro-Typography (Data & Telemetry)
nodes.rationale: Generous tracking (0.05em-0.1em) on small fixed monospace simulates mechanical typewriter spacing and terminal matrices.

nodes.label: Textural Contrast (High-Contrast Serif Disruption)
nodes.rationale: Serifs must be halftoned or 1-bit dithered to degrade vector perfection and create textural juxtaposition against clean sans-serifs.

nodes.label: Aviation/Hazard Red Accent (#E61919)
nodes.rationale: The single permitted accent across both substrates, reserved for strike-throughs, structural dividing lines, and vital data highlights.

nodes.label: The Blueprint Grid & Visible Compartmentalization
nodes.rationale: Elements anchor to grid tracks rather than float, and border-radius is absolutely rejected so all corners stay at 90 degrees for mechanical rigidity.

nodes.label: Bimodal Density
nodes.rationale: Layouts oscillate between packed monospace metadata clusters and vast negative space framing macro-typography, producing the declassified-document rhythm.

nodes.label: ASCII Syntax Decoration & Industrial Markers
nodes.rationale: Registration/copyright/trademark symbols are repurposed as structural geometric elements rather than legal text.

nodes.label: Analog Degradation Effects (Halftone, Scanlines, Noise)
nodes.rationale: Simulated hardware limitations are engineered in via CSS/SVG filters to stop the design from reading as purely digital.

nodes.label: Grid Determinism (gap:1px hairlines)
nodes.rationale: Using display:grid with gap:1px and contrasting parent/child backgrounds yields razor-thin dividers without complex border declarations.

nodes.label: minimalist-ui Skill (Premium Utilitarian Minimalism)
nodes.rationale: Targets document-style workspace-platform interfaces and actively rejects standard generic SaaS design trends.

nodes.label: Absolute Negative Constraints (Banned Elements)
nodes.rationale: Bans Inter/Roboto/Open Sans, Lucide/Feather icons, Tailwind heavy shadows, gradients, glassmorphism, rounded-full containers, emojis, placeholder names, and AI copy clichés as the fingerprint of generated design.

nodes.label: Minimalist Typographic Architecture
nodes.rationale: Pairs a geometric sans UI face with an editorial serif for hero headings and a mono for metadata; body text is never absolute black to avoid harsh contrast.

nodes.label: Warm Monochrome Palette + Spot Pastels
nodes.rationale: Color is treated as a scarce resource used only for semantic meaning, so accents are limited to washed-out pastel pairs with matched text colors.

nodes.label: Bento Box Feature Grid
nodes.rationale: Asymmetrical CSS Grid with strict 1px #EAEAEA borders and 8-12px radius keeps structure crisp without shadow-based elevation.

nodes.label: Iconography & Imagery Directives
nodes.rationale: Phosphor/Radix icons replace thin-line default sets; photography is desaturated and warm-grained so images dissolve into the monochrome palette.

nodes.label: Subtle Motion & Micro-Animations
nodes.rationale: Motion should feel invisible — quiet sophistication rather than spectacle; IntersectionObserver replaces scroll listeners and only transform/opacity are animated for GPU safety.

nodes.label: Minimalist Execution Protocol
nodes.rationale: Macro-whitespace is established first because vertical rhythm, not decoration, is what makes the editorial aesthetic read as premium.

nodes.label: Scan / Diagnose / Fix Sequence
nodes.rationale: Audit-first, improve-in-place: rewriting from scratch is banned so existing functionality and the existing stack survive the upgrade.

nodes.label: Purple/Blue AI Gradient Fingerprint
nodes.rationale: Named explicitly as the most common AI design fingerprint; the prescribed fix is a neutral base plus one considered accent.

nodes.label: Layout Audit
nodes.rationale: Three equal card columns is called the most generic AI layout; optical alignment fixes are demanded because mathematical centering often looks wrong.

nodes.label: Content Audit
nodes.rationale: Organic messy data (47.2%, +1 (312) 847-1928) reads as real, while round numbers and Acme-style names betray generated content.

nodes.label: Component Patterns Audit
nodes.rationale: Cards should exist only when elevation communicates hierarchy; otherwise border+shadow+white is decoration masquerading as structure.

nodes.label: Code Quality Audit
nodes.rationale: Includes an import-hallucination check against package.json, acknowledging that generated code frequently references nonexistent dependencies.

nodes.label: Fix Priority Order
nodes.rationale: Ordered for maximum visual impact at minimum risk — font swap first because it is the biggest instant improvement and lowest-risk change.

nodes.label: Stack Preservation Rules
nodes.rationale: No framework migration, no library additions before checking the dependency file, and Tailwind v3 vs v4 must be verified before touching config.

nodes.label: stitch-design-taste Skill
nodes.rationale: Translates anti-slop frontend directives into Stitch's native semantic 'Visual Descriptions' language, because Stitch interprets design through descriptive prose plus precise values.

nodes.label: Stitch MCP Server
nodes.rationale: Optional programmatic integration path for Cursor, Antigravity, or Gemini CLI.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md Output Format
nodes.rationale: The generated file is the single source of truth for prompting Stitch, so it must encode atmosphere, tokens, components, layout, motion and bans in one document.

nodes.label: Atmosphere Dials (Density / Variance / Motion)
nodes.rationale: Default baseline Variance 8, Motion 6, Density 4 — evocative adjective bands make taste communicable to a generative agent.

nodes.label: Color Calibration Constraints
nodes.rationale: Max one accent under 80% saturation, neutral Zinc/Slate bases, no AI purple/blue neon, and never pure #000000.

nodes.label: Stitch Typography Rules (Inter & Serif Bans)
nodes.rationale: Inter is banned for premium contexts to force unique character; generic serifs are banned outright and always banned in dashboards regardless of context.

nodes.label: Inline Image Typography (Hero Signature Technique)
nodes.rationale: Photos embedded at type-height between headline words act as visual punctuation — the identified signature creative move that separates the system from generic heroes.

nodes.label: No-Overlap Spatial Separation Principle
nodes.rationale: Every element must occupy its own clean spatial zone; absolute-positioned content stacking is banned because it degrades legibility and responsive behavior.

nodes.label: Stitch Layout Principles
nodes.rationale: min-h-[100dvh] replaces h-screen specifically because of the iOS Safari address-bar viewport jump.

nodes.label: Motion Philosophy (Spring Physics, Perpetual Micro-Loops)
nodes.rationale: Spring stiffness 100 / damping 20 gives a premium weighty feel; linear easing is banned and only transform/opacity may be animated.

nodes.label: Stitch Anti-Patterns (AI Tells)
nodes.rationale: The anti-pattern list is described as what actually makes output premium — encoding the bans matters as much as encoding the rules.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md — Design System: Taste Standard
nodes.rationale: The concrete reference instance of the DESIGN.md format produced by the stitch-design-taste skill.

nodes.label: Configuration Dials (Creativity / Density / Variance / Motion Intent)
nodes.rationale: Creativity 8 / Density 4 / Variance 8 / Motion 6 defaults; low creativity yields Notion-like quiet UI while high creativity unlocks inline image typography and editorial asymmetry.

nodes.label: Color Palette & Roles
nodes.rationale: Each token carries a descriptive name, hex, and functional role so a generative agent can reason about purpose rather than appearance.

nodes.label: Accent Selection (Pick ONE)
nodes.rationale: Four accents mapped to product domains (Emerald=growth, Electric Blue=SaaS/dev, Deep Rose=editorial, Amber=community) so accent choice is semantic, not decorative.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md Component Stylings
nodes.rationale: Cards only when elevation communicates hierarchy; high-density layouts drop cards for border-top dividers or negative space.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md Hero Section
nodes.rationale: Filler chrome such as 'Scroll to explore' and bouncing chevrons is banned on the reasoning that the user already knows how to scroll.

nodes.label: Bento Architecture & Layout Principles
nodes.rationale: Row 1 three columns / Row 2 two columns at 70-30 replaces the banned three-equal-card feature row, with a perpetual micro-animation per tile.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md Responsive Rules
nodes.rationale: Responsive is a hard requirement verified at 375/390/768/1024/1440px; any horizontal overflow on mobile is treated as a critical failure.

nodes.label: DESIGN.md Motion & Interaction (Code-Phase Intent)
nodes.rationale: Stitch generates static screens and cannot animate, so motion is documented as intent for the downstream coding agent (Antigravity, Cursor) to implement.
